world.title: Macron hosts Carney in French archipelago near Canada
world.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Saint Pierre and Miquelon on Saturday, September 19, for a three-day visit during which he was to host Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday. The meeting is the first visit by a Canadian prime minister to the French archipelago, which lies about 20 to 25 kilometers of
world.content: French President Emmanuel Macron arrived in Saint Pierre and Miquelon on Saturday, September 19, for a three-day visit during which he was to host Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Sunday. The meeting is the first visit by a Canadian prime minister to the French archipelago, which lies about 20 to 25 kilometers off Newfoundland and has fewer than 6,000 residents. Macron is the first French president to visit since François Hollande traveled there in 2014. The visit followed a social-media image posted by President Donald Trump that showed Saint Pierre and Miquelon and other territories under the U.S. flag; Macron responded upon arrival by reaffirming that the archipelago is French. Canada and the EU are discussing a closer relationship after European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen proposed associate-member status for Canada.

world.title: Turkey offers Saudi military support under Makkah pact
world.summary: Turkey said it could help meet Saudi Arabia’s military needs under a trilateral defense pact with Pakistan, following escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Saudi Arabia could require assistance, particularly on technical matters, and Ankara could provide it under the agreement. Fid
world.content: Turkey said it could help meet Saudi Arabia’s military needs under a trilateral defense pact with Pakistan, following escalating Houthi attacks on the kingdom. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Saudi Arabia could require assistance, particularly on technical matters, and Ankara could provide it under the agreement. Fidan said it was unacceptable to draw Saudi Arabia into the United States-Iran war because Riyadh did not want to join the conflict. He said proposals had been sent to all sides to end the fighting but did not disclose their contents, adding that the conflict’s economic effects had become intolerable. Pakistan has said it has not discussed a military response under the pact.

world.title: Iran sends seven conditions to restart U.S. peace talks
world.summary: Iran sent the United States seven conditions for restarting negotiations to end the war, conveyed through Qatari mediators, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said Sept. 19. He identified three demands: an end to fighting on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian funds and the lifting
world.content: Iran sent the United States seven conditions for restarting negotiations to end the war, conveyed through Qatari mediators, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, said Sept. 19. He identified three demands: an end to fighting on all fronts, the release of frozen Iranian funds and the lifting of the U.S. naval blockade of Iranian ports. Tehran is awaiting President Donald Trump’s response as consultations continue with Qatar and Pakistan. Rezaei said Iran would not accept negotiations unless its conditions were met and warned that Tehran was prepared for a “decisive war.” The statement followed the collapse of a June framework that gave the parties 60 days to negotiate a permanent settlement. The deadline expired in August without an agreement, while disputes over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz continued. Iran has also sought an end to fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.
world.image_alt: Iran sends seven conditions to restart U.S. peace talks

world.title: Israeli president clears soldier’s record over 2016 Hebron killing
world.summary: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday pardoned former combat medic Elor Azaria and shortened the waiting period for the erasure of his criminal record, effectively clearing it nearly a decade after Azaria was convicted of manslaughter for killing Abdel Fattah al-Sharif in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank. Al-Shar
world.content: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Saturday pardoned former combat medic Elor Azaria and shortened the waiting period for the erasure of his criminal record, effectively clearing it nearly a decade after Azaria was convicted of manslaughter for killing Abdel Fattah al-Sharif in Hebron, in the occupied West Bank. Al-Sharif had stabbed and wounded an Israeli soldier before Israeli forces shot him, leaving him injured and incapacitated; a cellphone video showed Azaria approaching and firing a shot into his head. Herzog’s office cited the time elapsed, Azaria’s completion of his sentence, remorse he had expressed and the approaching Yom Kippur holiday. The decision followed a recommendation from Defense Minister Israel Katz. IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir opposed it, saying Azaria had not shown remorse or accepted responsibility for his actions.

world.title: US strike kills four on alleged drug boat in Caribbean
world.summary: The U.S. military said it struck a fast boat in the Caribbean on Saturday, Sept. 19, killing four people it identified as “narco-terrorists.” U.S. Southern Command said confirmed intelligence showed the vessel was actively involved in drug trafficking and operating along established smuggling routes. The Joint Task For
world.content: The U.S. military said it struck a fast boat in the Caribbean on Saturday, Sept. 19, killing four people it identified as “narco-terrorists.” U.S. Southern Command said confirmed intelligence showed the vessel was actively involved in drug trafficking and operating along established smuggling routes. The Joint Task Force Western Hemisphere carried out the attack under SOUTHCOM’s direction. The operation is part of the Trump administration’s campaign against suspected cartel-linked vessels in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. The latest strike brought the reported death toll to at least 231 people in 69 strikes over roughly a year. The military did not provide evidence that the targeted boat was carrying drugs; a released video showed a moving vessel followed by a flash. Rights groups and legal experts have described the attacks as possible extrajudicial killings, and the U.N. human rights chief previously called for independent investigations.
world.image_alt: US strike kills four on alleged drug boat in Caribbean

world.title: German state elections test Chancellor Merz after AfD surge
world.summary: Voters in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania began voting Sunday in regional elections that could increase pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz and his Christian Democratic Union (CDU). The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is seeking further gains two weeks after winning 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt, its strong
world.content: Voters in Berlin and Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania began voting Sunday in regional elections that could increase pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz and his Christian Democratic Union (CDU). The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) is seeking further gains two weeks after winning 43.8% in Saxony-Anhalt, its strongest result in a state election; the CDU received about 17% there. Merz has been chancellor for 16 months, and his approval rating has fallen to roughly 13% to 14% in recent surveys. In Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania, polls put the center-left Social Democrats (SPD) and AfD in a close contest, while the CDU risks falling below the 5% threshold for representation. In Berlin, Die Linke leads the CDU narrowly in several polls, with the AfD also positioned to make gains. Merz called a CDU crisis meeting, cleared his schedule and canceled a planned trip to the United Nations General Assembly to respond to the results. He has resisted calls to resign as he struggles to advance promised economic and social-welfare reforms with the SPD.
world.image_alt: German state elections test Chancellor Merz after AfD surge

world.title: Russian authorities say Ukrainian drones hit Moscow refinery during elections
world.summary: Russian authorities said Ukraine launched a large-scale drone attack on Moscow and the surrounding region early Sunday, killing two people, injuring six and damaging a facility at the Moscow Oil Refinery. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted across Russia since Saturday, includi
world.content: Russian authorities said Ukraine launched a large-scale drone attack on Moscow and the surrounding region early Sunday, killing two people, injuring six and damaging a facility at the Moscow Oil Refinery. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted across Russia since Saturday, including 450 approaching the capital. Moscow Region Governor Andrei Vorobyov separately reported 249 drones shot down over 17 districts. The claims could not be independently verified, and Ukraine did not immediately comment. The attack took place on the final day of Russia’s three-day parliamentary election. Authorities said a 44-year-old woman died when a drone hit a residential building in Sofyino, and an elderly man died after a private home was struck in Orekhovo-Zuyevo. Falling debris started a fire at a 21-story apartment block in Ramenskoye, prompting the evacuation of about 400 people, including 70 children. Moscow airports imposed temporary flight restrictions as emergency crews responded to fires and damage in residential and industrial areas.
world.image_alt: Russian authorities say Ukrainian drones hit Moscow refinery during elections

world.title: Dutch police disperse far-right rally after violence in The Hague
world.summary: Dutch riot police dispersed about 500 far-right protesters in The Hague on Saturday, Sept. 19, after demonstrators at Malieveld park threw fireworks and other projectiles at officers during a rally against immigration and asylum policies. Authorities banned a planned march through the city, ordered the gathering to dis
world.content: Dutch riot police dispersed about 500 far-right protesters in The Hague on Saturday, Sept. 19, after demonstrators at Malieveld park threw fireworks and other projectiles at officers during a rally against immigration and asylum policies. Authorities banned a planned march through the city, ordered the gathering to disperse, and used baton charges, police dogs, mounted officers and water cannon. Police said they arrested 24 people. Protesters gave Nazi salutes and shouted antisemitic slogans, according to Justice Minister David van Weel and Prime Minister Rob Jetten. Van Weel called for an “extremely firm” response, while Jetten said protesters had deliberately sought confrontation with police. The municipality said calm returned after the crowd was moved away from the Malieveld.
world.image_alt: Dutch police disperse far-right rally after violence in The Hague

business.title: EU fuel prices reach records as diesel margins are expected to peak in October
business.summary: Average petrol and diesel prices across the European Union reached record highs this week, with petrol at €2.063 per litre and diesel at €2.159 on September 14, according to European Commission data. Filling a 50-litre tank cost about €103 with petrol and €108 with diesel. Refining margins, which reflect the cost of co
business.content: Average petrol and diesel prices across the European Union reached record highs this week, with petrol at €2.063 per litre and diesel at €2.159 on September 14, according to European Commission data. Filling a 50-litre tank cost about €103 with petrol and €108 with diesel. Refining margins, which reflect the cost of converting crude oil into fuel, are contributing to the increase. European Central Bank experts told Euronews that diesel margins are not expected to peak until October. Fuel prices have risen since conflict in the Middle East disrupted energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz. Eurozone energy inflation increased to 14.3% in August from 10.3% in July, while the weighted average EU petrol price has risen about 29% since the start of 2026 and diesel nearly 40%.
business.image_alt: EU fuel prices reach records as diesel margins are expected to peak in October

business.title: U.S. and China open talks ahead of Trump-Xi summit
business.summary: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer are scheduled to meet in New York on Sunday to discuss artificial intelligence, trade, critical minerals and other economic issues, according to statements and people familiar with the plans. The meeting i
business.content: U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer are scheduled to meet in New York on Sunday to discuss artificial intelligence, trade, critical minerals and other economic issues, according to statements and people familiar with the plans. The meeting is intended to prepare for President Donald Trump’s Sept. 24 summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington. The negotiators are expected to address whether to extend a tariff truce that expires Nov. 10, Chinese controls on rare-earth and other critical-mineral shipments, technology and investment issues, and disruptions linked to the Iran war. The United States also wants to monitor existing commitments and improve market access for American farmers, manufacturers and workers, according to the U.S. trade representative’s office.

business.title: Goldman links weak consumer sentiment to lower happiness
business.summary: Goldman Sachs economist Joseph Briggs said consumer sentiment remains deeply pessimistic even though the economy appears solid by conventional measures, CNBC reported on Sept. 19. Briggs attributed part of the gap to broader pessimism in society and what he described as lower happiness. A Reddit discussion responding t
business.content: Goldman Sachs economist Joseph Briggs said consumer sentiment remains deeply pessimistic even though the economy appears solid by conventional measures, CNBC reported on Sept. 19. Briggs attributed part of the gap to broader pessimism in society and what he described as lower happiness. A Reddit discussion responding to the report argued that affordability pressures, including grocery costs, better explain why people feel financially strained; those claims appeared in a user-generated post rather than in the supplied CNBC report.

business.title: California billionaire wealth tax gains Nobel economists’ support
business.summary: Six Nobel Prize-winning economists have endorsed California’s Proposition 40, a ballot initiative that would impose a one-time tax equal to 5% of the assets of residents worth more than $1 billion. The signatories are Daron Acemoglu, Abhijit Banerjee, Peter Diamond, Esther Duflo, Paul Krugman and Joseph Stiglitz. They
business.content: Six Nobel Prize-winning economists have endorsed California’s Proposition 40, a ballot initiative that would impose a one-time tax equal to 5% of the assets of residents worth more than $1 billion. The signatories are Daron Acemoglu, Abhijit Banerjee, Peter Diamond, Esther Duflo, Paul Krugman and Joseph Stiglitz. They estimate that California’s 250 billionaires collectively hold $2.3 trillion and that the state income taxes they paid between 2019 and 2025 equaled 1.6% of their $1.4 trillion increase in wealth. Supporters describe the measure as a possible model for wealth taxes in other U.S. states, the federal government and other countries. Opponents say it could damage economic growth, startups and company founders who might need to sell large stakes to pay the levy. A campaign led by Google co-founder Sergey Brin has raised $193 million to oppose the proposal, which is scheduled for a California vote on November 3, 2026.
business.image_alt: California billionaire wealth tax gains Nobel economists’ support

business.title: Iran war keeps oil volatile without feared price surge
business.summary: The six-month U.S.-Iran war has kept oil markets volatile but has not produced the more than twofold price increase energy analysts warned could follow a prolonged conflict. President Donald Trump launched the war in late February, and oil prices remain elevated as the conflict continues without a clear end.
business.content: The six-month U.S.-Iran war has kept oil markets volatile but has not produced the more than twofold price increase energy analysts warned could follow a prolonged conflict. Ethereum approached $2,620, while other cryptocurrencies and crypto-linked stocks also advanced. The rebound followed a hawkish Federal Reserve stance, uncertainty a
business.content: Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000, rising above $81,000 during Friday trading as exchange-traded-fund inflows and renewed institutional demand supported the move. Ethereum approached $2,620, while other cryptocurrencies and crypto-linked stocks also advanced. The rebound followed a hawkish Federal Reserve stance, uncertainty after the CLARITY Act setback and continuing U.S. regulatory changes. Market reports cited improving risk sentiment, lower oil prices and short-position liquidations as additional factors. Elevated interest rates, ETF outflows in some reports and regulatory uncertainty remained risks. The SEC and CFTC continued separate crypto-related initiatives despite the congressional setback.

business.title: AI subscribers sue four tech firms over alleged slowdown pact
business.summary: Four paid subscribers of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Gemini sued Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on Friday, alleging the companies coordinated to slow AI development in violation of antitrust law. The proposed nationwide class action argues that sl
business.content: Four paid subscribers of ChatGPT, Claude, Grok and Gemini sued Anthropic, OpenAI, SpaceXAI and Google in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California on Friday, alleging the companies coordinated to slow AI development in violation of antitrust law. The proposed nationwide class action argues that slower product improvements would reduce the value of paid subscriptions. The complaint identifies Sept. 12 as the date of the alleged coordination, after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay calling for industry cooperation to slow AI advances and strengthen safety measures. The filing says OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk and Google DeepMind chair Demis Hassabis publicly supported the proposal that day. The companies did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Amodei’s essay acknowledged potential antitrust issues and said government mediation or narrowly defined exemptions could enable safety discussions.
business.image_alt: AI subscribers sue four tech firms over alleged slowdown pact

science.title: NASA awards SpaceX $946 million for three ISS missions
science.summary: NASA has awarded SpaceX a $946 million contract modification for three additional astronaut missions to the International Space Station: Crew-15, Crew-16 and Crew-17. The missions expand SpaceX’s existing Commercial Crew Transportation Capability agreement to $5.92 billion across 17 flights. The agreement covers launch
science.content: NASA has awarded SpaceX a $946 million contract modification for three additional astronaut missions to the International Space Station: Crew-15, Crew-16 and Crew-17. The missions expand SpaceX’s existing Commercial Crew Transportation Capability agreement to $5.92 billion across 17 flights. The agreement covers launch, ground support, in-orbit operations, return, cargo transport and a docked lifeboat capability through 2030. Boeing’s Starliner remains grounded.
science.image_alt: NASA awards SpaceX $946 million for three ISS missions

science.title: Europe
science.summary: Europe experienced its warmest summer since records began in 2026, surpassing the previous record set in 2003, while extreme heat contributed to thousands of deaths. Germany's estimated heat-related death toll reached at least 16,300 by the end of August; the estimate includes deaths in which heat worsened underlying h
science.content: Europe experienced its warmest summer since records began in 2026, surpassing the previous record set in 2003, while extreme heat contributed to thousands of deaths. Germany's estimated heat-related death toll reached at least 16,300 by the end of August; the estimate includes deaths in which heat worsened underlying health conditions rather than directly causing death. Germany averaged about 22 days with temperatures of at least 30 degrees Celsius and about five days with temperatures of at least 35 degrees, according to the country's weather service. France experienced its most severe heatwave on record, with almost 8,000 excess deaths and about 120,000 hectares of land scorched.

science.title: Scientists propose lensing solution for impossible black hole merger
science.summary: Astronomers have proposed that gravitational lensing — the warping of light and other signals by massive objects — may explain why GW231123 appeared to involve unusually large black holes. The signal was detected in November 2023. GW231123 was described as the most massive black hole merger detected to date, but the ap
science.content: Astronomers have proposed that gravitational lensing — the warping of light and other signals by massive objects — may explain why GW231123 appeared to involve unusually large black holes. The signal was detected in November 2023. GW231123 was described as the most massive black hole merger detected to date, but the apparent masses of its component black holes were difficult to reconcile with existing expectations for black hole formation. The lensing proposal could account for the unusual measurement but raises a separate question about a previously unobserved type of spacetime distortion.
science.image_alt: Scientists propose lensing solution for impossible black hole merger

science.title: Europe counts €180bn damage after record-hot summer
science.summary: Europe experienced record-shattering heatwaves, wildfires, depleted rivers and reservoirs, crop losses, and infrastructure damage across the continent. France recorded its hottest day ever, and about 35,000 people in Europe died during the summer's extreme heat. The European Union estimated the damage at about €180 bil
science.content: Europe experienced record-shattering heatwaves, wildfires, depleted rivers and reservoirs, crop losses, and infrastructure damage across the continent. France recorded its hottest day ever, and about 35,000 people in Europe died during the summer's extreme heat. The European Union estimated the damage at about €180 billion. Harvest losses will probably raise food-price inflation, while infrastructure repairs have only just begun. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen called the season a “summer of truth”.
science.image_alt: Europe counts €180bn damage after record-hot summer

science.title: Bolivian researchers identify new wild-cat species, Leopardus tilcayo
science.summary: Researchers have formally identified Leopardus tilcayo, a previously unrecognized wild-cat species from Bolivia’s Yungas region. It is the first living wild-cat species named and described in more than a century. The small, spotted cat was living at the Senda Verde wildlife refuge after a local family found it in the f
science.content: Researchers have formally identified Leopardus tilcayo, a previously unrecognized wild-cat species from Bolivia’s Yungas region. It is the first living wild-cat species named and described in more than a century. The small, spotted cat was living at the Senda Verde wildlife refuge after a local family found it in the forest and initially kept it as a pet. Bolivian biologist Paola Nogales-Ascarrunz examined the animal after a colleague flagged its unusual appearance. Researchers compared whole-genome data from 38 tiger cats and related animals sampled across South America. Their analysis found that tiger cats previously treated as a single group represent five genetically distinct species and estimated that the L. tilcayo lineage split from other tiger cats about 1.4 million years ago. Current Biology published the peer-reviewed study Sept. 17.
science.image_alt: Bolivian researchers identify new wild-cat species, Leopardus tilcayo

science.title: Study finds distinct brain changes across female life stages
science.summary: A study found that puberty and pregnancy are associated with similar, widespread structural changes in the female brain, mainly reductions in gray matter. Researchers identified a different pattern during the menopausal transition: a pause in typical age-related brain changes rather than an acceleration. The study, pub
science.content: A study found that puberty and pregnancy are associated with similar, widespread structural changes in the female brain, mainly reductions in gray matter. Researchers identified a different pattern during the menopausal transition: a pause in typical age-related brain changes rather than an acceleration. The study, published in Nature Communications, compared brain remodeling across three major hormonal transitions: puberty, pregnancy and menopause. Menopause research has more often examined individual brain regions or compared different groups of women at one point in time.
science.image_alt: Study finds distinct brain changes across female life stages

science.title: Researchers build DNA computer for 100-bit calculations
science.summary: Researchers at Maynooth University in Ireland have built a programmable DNA computer that performs calculations using billions of molecules in a drop of water. The system, called a Scaffolded DNA Computer, performs arithmetic without electricity or a continuous external energy supply. DNA molecules compete for binding
science.content: Researchers at Maynooth University in Ireland have built a programmable DNA computer that performs calculations using billions of molecules in a drop of water. The system, called a Scaffolded DNA Computer, performs arithmetic without electricity or a continuous external energy supply. DNA molecules compete for binding sites on a molecular scaffold, and the energetically favorable binding outcome represents the answer. The computer ran 10 molecular programs, including complex 100-bit calculations. Researchers designed the system with DNA origami software, which maps a long DNA strand into a scaffold that organizes shorter strands for computation. Damien Woods of Maynooth University said the competitive binding process both selects the winning molecular configuration and processes information.
science.image_alt: Researchers build DNA computer for 100-bit calculations

science.title: International Observe the Moon Night draws global skywatchers
science.summary: International Observe the Moon Night was scheduled for Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, inviting people worldwide to observe Earth’s nearest celestial neighbor with telescopes and other activities. The annual event has been held since 2010 and is scheduled near the Moon’s first-quarter phase, when sunlight creates long shadow
science.content: International Observe the Moon Night was scheduled for Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026, inviting people worldwide to observe Earth’s nearest celestial neighbor with telescopes and other activities. The annual event has been held since 2010 and is scheduled near the Moon’s first-quarter phase, when sunlight creates long shadows that make craters, ridges and mountain peaks easier to see. In September 2026, the Moon reached its first-quarter phase on Sept. 18, leaving a waxing gibbous Moon visible during the event the following evening. Western Nevada College’s Jack C. Davis Observatory scheduled a free viewing session at 6:30 p.m., led by observatory director Thomas Herring, who was also slated to discuss lunar history, statistics and NASA’s Artemis effort to return astronauts to the Moon.
science.image_alt: International Observe the Moon Night draws global skywatchers

sports.title: Vanderbilt rallies past NC State on final-second fumble
sports.summary: Vanderbilt defeated NC State 35-31 in Nashville on Sept. 19 after Cayden Daniels recovered a fumble in the end zone with one second remaining for the winning touchdown. NC State led 31-28 and was positioned to run out the clock, but quarterback CJ Bailey fumbled while attempting to take an intentional safety. The Commo
sports.content: Vanderbilt defeated NC State 35-31 in Nashville on Sept. 19 after Cayden Daniels recovered a fumble in the end zone with one second remaining for the winning touchdown. NC State led 31-28 and was positioned to run out the clock, but quarterback CJ Bailey fumbled while attempting to take an intentional safety. The Commodores rallied after trailing 17-0 and 24-7, while NC State held the lead for nearly the entire game. Vanderbilt quarterback Jared Curtis threw a late interception at the NC State 2-yard line before Miles Capers forced Bailey’s fumble, allowing Daniels to score.

sports.summary: Joey Logano won Saturday night’s NASCAR Cup Series race at Bristol Motor Speedway after leading the final seven laps. Carson Hocevar and Ryan Blaney exchanged punches on pit road after a late-race collision. Hocevar finished third, Kyle Larson was second, and the altercation drew attention after Logano’s victory. Hocev
sports.content: Joey Logano won Saturday night’s NASCAR Cup Series race at Bristol Motor Speedway after leading the final seven laps. Carson Hocevar and Ryan Blaney exchanged punches on pit road after a late-race collision. Hocevar finished third, Kyle Larson was second, and the altercation drew attention after Logano’s victory. Hocevar and Blaney made contact while racing for second with about 41–43 laps remaining. Blaney, who led 202 laps and won Stage 2, crashed into the outside wall and finished 33rd. After the race, Blaney approached Hocevar’s car, and the drivers exchanged punches before crews and officials separated them.

sports.title: Raphinha hat-trick keeps Barcelona perfect against Sevilla
sports.summary: Barcelona came from behind to beat Sevilla 3-1 at the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán on September 19, with captain Raphinha scoring all three goals. Youssouf Fofana headed Sevilla ahead in the 19th minute, but Raphinha equalized three minutes later before adding a header in the 52nd minute and completing his hat-trick in the 69
sports.content: Barcelona came from behind to beat Sevilla 3-1 at the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán on September 19, with captain Raphinha scoring all three goals. Youssouf Fofana headed Sevilla ahead in the 19th minute, but Raphinha equalized three minutes later before adding a header in the 52nd minute and completing his hat-trick in the 69th. The result gave Hansi Flick’s defending champions seven wins from seven LaLiga matches and 21 points, six ahead of second-placed Real Madrid before Madrid’s September 20 derby against Atlético. Raphinha leads the league scoring chart with 12 goals in seven appearances after moving into a central-striker role, while Barcelona sporting director Deco confirmed that the Brazil international had agreed to extend his contract through 2030.
sports.image_alt: Raphinha hat-trick keeps Barcelona perfect against Sevilla

sports.title: Newcastle defeat Hull 2-1 to end unbeaten start
sports.summary: Newcastle United beat Hull City 2-1 at St James’ Park on Saturday, ending the newly promoted side’s unbeaten Premier League start. Joe Willock put Newcastle ahead after three minutes, and Lewis Hall doubled the lead four minutes later, with Harvey Barnes creating both goals. Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis saved
sports.content: Newcastle United beat Hull City 2-1 at St James’ Park on Saturday, ending the newly promoted side’s unbeaten Premier League start. Joe Willock put Newcastle ahead after three minutes, and Lewis Hall doubled the lead four minutes later, with Harvey Barnes creating both goals. Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis saved a first-half penalty from Yoane Wissa. Hull improved after the break, and Mohamed-Ali Cho reduced the deficit in the 67th minute, but Newcastle held off a late push to secure their second league win. Both clubs have eight points from five matches, while Hull suffered their first defeat of the campaign.
sports.image_alt: Newcastle defeat Hull 2-1 to end unbeaten start

sports.title: Manchester United Muslim supporters call for Ratcliffe, Glazers to leave
sports.summary: Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club has called for co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family to leave the club after Ratcliffe said in a BBC interview that the UK was declining because of high taxes and high immigration. The group issued a statement of no confidence, describing his latest comments as “deepl
sports.content: Manchester United Muslim Supporters Club has called for co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazer family to leave the club after Ratcliffe said in a BBC interview that the UK was declining because of high taxes and high immigration. The group issued a statement of no confidence, describing his latest comments as “deeply disappointing and completely unacceptable”. MUMSC said Manchester United’s players, staff, stewards, security teams and supporters come from different countries, cultures, ethnicities, religions and backgrounds, and argued that the club’s identity should not be reduced to its investors. Ratcliffe acquired a 27.7% stake in 2024 and previously apologised after saying Britain had been “colonised by immigrants”; the club said at the time that it prides itself on being inclusive.
sports.image_alt: Manchester United Muslim supporters call for Ratcliffe, Glazers to leave

sports.title: England reclaim T20 top spot after Sri Lanka sweep
sports.summary: England reclaimed the No. 1 position in the men’s T20 international rankings with an eight-wicket win over Sri Lanka at Old Trafford on September 19, completing a 3-0 series whitewash. sports.content: England reclaimed the No. 1 position in the men’s T20 international rankings with an eight-wicket win over Sri Lanka at Old Trafford on September 19, completing a 3-0 series whitewash. sports.content: Rory McIlroy moved into contention for the BMW PGA Championship at Wentworth after closing his third round with an eagle on the par-five 18th. The Northern Irishman shot a three-under 69 to reach 11 under par, two shots behind Spain’s Manuel Elvira and Italy’s Filippo Celli, who both birdied the final hole to share the lead at 13 under. McIlroy was one over par through 11 holes before birdies at the 12th and 17th set up his finish. He is tied for sixth with Adam Scott, Joaquin Niemann, Davis Bryant and Kristoffer Reitan heading into Sunday’s final round, as difficult, shifting winds kept the leaderboard tightly packed.

sports.content: Coventry City beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 at the City Ground on 19 September for their first Premier League win since April 2001 and their first points of the 2026-27 campaign. Jay Dasilva scored in the 55th minute after controlling goalkeeper Carl Rushworth’s long pass and finishing beyond Matz Sels. The promoted side had opened the season with four defeats and no goals but defended their lead through sustained Forest pressure. Referee Jared Gillett overturned Igor Jesus’ late equaliser after a VAR review found a foul on Coventry’s Caleb Yirenkyi in the build-up.
